description: Backlog #3012 — the committed, inspectable classifier behind the progress board's weekly product-vs-machinery output ratio. Every line added to this repository is charged to exactly ONE of three classes by the FIRST rule below whose `match` accepts its path: `product` (the thing the repo exists to ship), `machinery` (the delivery loop and its backlog bookkeeping), or `other` (deliberately counted in neither). Order is load-bearing — the exclusions come first so a generated file inside `src/` is never credited as product. Nothing is classified by a regex buried in a function: to disagree with the number, open this file, change one rule's `class`, and re-run `node scripts/progress-board.mjs`. Each rule carries a `why` that is the whole explanation for that path, so `classifyPath()` can answer 'why is this file machinery?' in one line.

conventions.matching: First match wins, top to bottom. `**` matches any characters including `/`; `*` matches any characters except `/`; everything else is literal. Paths are repo-relative, forward-slashed, exactly as `git log --numstat` reports them (the NEW path, for a rename).
conventions.counting: Only ADDED lines are counted — the metric is output, not churn, so a deletion is not negative output. Binary files (`-` in numstat) contribute 0.
conventions.tests: Test lines are charged to the thing they test, never to a class of their own. `scripts/**` therefore absorbs `scripts/__tests__/**` and `scripts/lib/__tests__/**` as machinery, while `tests/**` and any `*.test.ts` under `blocks/`/`demos/` count as product. Change this by adding a rule ABOVE the group you want to carve out of.
conventions.generated: Generated and vendored files are `other`, not `product` or `machinery` — nobody authored those lines, so crediting them to either side inflates that week's output. Each generated-file rule names the command that writes it, so the list can be re-checked when a generator moves.
conventions.default: A path matching no rule falls to `other`. `other` is reported alongside the two headline numbers precisely so the reader can see how much of the tree the classification does NOT cover — a large `other` is a signal that this file needs a new rule, not that the metric is wrong.
conventions.knownGap: READ THIS BEFORE CITING THE PRODUCT NUMBER. The default is NOT symmetric between the two headline classes, and the asymmetry runs in one direction. Machinery lives in a small, stable, fully-covered set of directories (scripts/, backlog/, .claude/, skills-src/, agent-memory-src/, docs/, .github/, .githooks/, tools/), so machinery coverage is effectively complete. Product does not: the `product` rules cover FOUR directories (src/, blocks/, demos/, tests/), while the standard's own declarations live in ~45 further top-level domain directories — `contracts/`, `capabilities/`, `conformance-vectors/`, `webcases/`, `validation-generation/`, `capability-manifest/`, and the per-domain `<domain>/contract.ts` trees (intl/, webtheme/, permissions/, positioning/, realtime/, …). Those are unmatched today and fall to `other`: 38,852 tracked lines at the 2026-08-09 HEAD, and roughly 730 of the added lines in the five measured weeks. So the published `product` figure is a LOWER BOUND and the machinery:product ratio is an UPPER bound. Whether those directories are `product` is an operator call that has not been made; `uncoveredTopLevel` in the test suite pins the gap so a NEW uncovered directory fails loudly instead of silently joining the remainder.

rules.why: lockfile — npm writes every line of it, so it is nobody's output
generated by `npm run gen:cem` (scripts/gen-cem.mjs)
generated by `npm run gen:reference-index` (scripts/gen-reference-index.mjs) — inside src/, so this rule must stay above the src/ product rule
generated by `npm run gen:maas-openapi` (scripts/gen-maas-openapi.mjs) — inside blocks/, so it must stay above the blocks/ product rule
generated by `npm run gen:webdirectives-ssr-vectors` (scripts/gen-webdirectives-ssr-vectors.mjs)
vendored copy of the plugs runtime that Frontier UI owns (#606); deleted from this tree by #1504, kept as a rule so historical weeks never credit WE with another repo's code
backlog bookkeeping — one markdown card per work item, the tracker itself
delivery machinery — the scripts that run the loop, including their own __tests__ (tests of machinery are machinery)
build and delivery tooling
agent harness — hooks, commands and settings that drive the loop
agent skills; `.claude/skills` is a symlink to this directory (scripts/sync-skills-deploy.mjs), so this is the same machinery as .claude/ with a different home
agent memory source, deployed into the harness — instructions to the loop, not product

the lane transport's own bookkeeping — written by scripts/lane-pool.mjs and dropped again at land (#2288); it was the single largest unclassified contributor before this rule (+1,170 lines over 2026-07-06..2026-08-09)
agent operating instructions

the rest of docs/ is delivery-side too — design notes and mocks for the agent surfaces (docs/design/**). An earlier revision asserted 'the whole of docs/ is docs/agent/ today', which is true of the HEAD tree but was NOT true of the measured window: +1,033 lines of docs/design/ landed in the week of 2026-07-13 and fell to `other` against that stated intent
CI workflows and issue templates — the delivery pipeline
git hooks that gate the loop
the standard's spec data (src/_data/*.json, src/_includes/*-descriptions) plus the 11ty site that renders it — WE's actual shipped surface
block implementations and their per-block protocols
runtime conformance demos and exercise apps — the executable half of the standard
tests of the product surface; test lines count with the thing they test
analysis and review write-ups — neither product code nor delivery machinery; stated explicitly rather than left to the default so the choice is visible and arguable
